processes.name: Actual Costing
processes.overview: This solution process enables actual costing for material inventory. Initially, all goods movements in a period are valuated based on standard price. All price and exchange rate differences for the material are collected in the material ledger. Similarly, all confirmations are valuated based on a standard activity rate. At the end of the period, an actual price (called the periodic unit price) is calculated for each material based on actual costs within the period, and an actual activity rate is calculated based on the actual costs for the cost center. This calculated actual price can then be used to revalue inventory, COGS and WIP at period end. For actual costing, to calculate the periodic unit price for your materials, you need to activate actual costing in addition to the material ledger. You also need to choose single-level or multilevel price determination for your materials and use price control standard price for all materials you want to use in actual costing.

processes.name: Automotive Supply to Customer – Inventory Management
processes.overview: This scope item validates the execution of an end-to-end automotive supply-to-customer process, focusing on integrated activities across procurement, production, delivery, billing, and payment, with full inventory management support. The process begins with creating a sales scheduling agreement and maintaining forecast delivery schedules. Planning delivery schedules can be generated to smooth demand for production. Just-in-Time (JIT) calls, which include component details and requirements, can be created manually. Components are planned and procured through material requirements planning (MRP) and purchase scheduling agreements with external suppliers. Inbound deliveries are created, goods receipts are posted, and supplier invoices are generated. MRP also generates planned orders for production. Repetitive manufacturing confirmation triggers activities like finished goods receipt, component backflush, and cost posting. For JIT calls, production-relevant components or package units are released. Outbound deliveries to customers are created based on open quantities. After picking and packing, the goods issue is posted. Goods can be posted as consignment stock, stored at the customer location but owned by suppliers. As goods are consumed, customers send JIT delivery confirmations via the SOAP API, or a consignment issue order is created manually. Delivery confirmations are matched with existing JIT call deliveries, and once released, subsequent documents are created, and the goods issue is posted. Deliveries can be invoiced once goods are delivered. All incoming and outgoing payments are posted, and all products in this scenario are inventory managed.

processes.name: Basic Available-to-Promise Processing
processes.overview: A product availability check can be executed for planned orders, production orders, deliveries, sales orders, and stock transport orders, resulting in the order document containing one or more confirmed schedule lines. If the available quantity of a material is insufficient to fulfill requirements, backorder processing can be performed for sales orders or stock transport orders in alignment with a specific business strategy. Backorder processing is scheduled to run automatically and periodically, resulting in the generation of reprioritized requirements. processes.name: Batch Derivation – Consumer Products
processes.overview: This document outlines the production and packaging processes in the Consumer Products Industry, focusing on batch derivation of the earliest manufacturing date from component batches to the produced material. Condition records maintain the relevant inheritance characteristics. The goods receipt posting of finished products after production serves as a derivation event. Batch derivation can be performed at one or more manufacturing levels, with two alternative processes described: a single-step and a two-step batch derivation. At the start, you choose between these alternatives by selecting a corresponding production version. The process begins with creating a demand forecast for finished goods, represented by Planned Independent Requirements (PIRs). Based on PIRs, Material Requirements Planning (MRP) generates a production plan for finished goods and explodes the entire bill of material structure. This results in planned production for finished products, semifinished products (in two-step batch derivation), and purchase requirements. In the two-step batch derivation process, production starts with converting a planned order into a process order or directly creating a process order for the semifinished product. The goods issue of components (one or more batches per component), production confirmation, and goods receipt of the semifinished product are then executed. The packing process applies to both single-level and two-step batch derivation. It begins with converting a planned order to a process order or directly creating a process order for the finished product. The goods issue of components, production confirmation, and goods receipt of the finished product follow. You can check the results of the one-step or two-level batch derivation in the derivation monitor. The Batch Cockpit is available for batch traceability checks. Manual derivation is possible but not included in this scenario.

processes.name: Business Partners for Retail
processes.overview: A supplier or vendor is a business partner who delivers and sells goods and services to a retailer. A supplier master holds information about the supplier such as its name, address, bank details, tax details, and billing preferences. This supplier information is used and stored in transactions such as purchase orders, goods receipts, and supplier invoices. Some supplier information is specific to a company (known as the company code) or purchasing unit (known as the purchasing organization) within a retailer’s organization. A customer is a business partner to which goods and services are sold and delivered. A customer master holds information about the customer such as its name, address, bank details, tax details, and delivery and billing preferences. This customer information is used and stored in transactions such as sales orders, deliveries, and billing documents. Some customer information is specific to a company (known as the company code) or sales unit (known as the sales area) within a retailer’s organization. Business partners have several different functions, described as partner functions. For example, typical partner functions for a supplier are ordering address, goods supplier, invoicing party. A business partner can be a customer and a supplier at the same time if, for example, the customer also supplies goods or if a supplier is also a customer. For internal suppliers and customers, see the Sites for Retail (3I3) scope item.

processes.name: Characteristic Value Conversion for Retail
processes.overview: In the retail and fashion industries, a characteristic of a product can be measured using different standards or scales in different countries or geographical regions. For example, a shoe that is considered size 9 in the UK may be a size 11 in the US. Hence, the shoe has both the sizes marked on it. To facilitate this, a characteristic conversion mechanism is necessary to ensure that on every product, sizes in all relevant size standards are correctly marked. Characteristic value conversion only applies to variant-creating characteristics that are attached to the article master. Characteristics refer to properties of an article such as the color of a shirt or the size of a shirt. The variant-creating characteristics are used to create variants of the generic product. The non-variant-creating characteristics are for information purposes only. Characteristic values are the attributes of a characteristic. For example, if the characteristic is color, the characteristic values can be red, blue, or yellow. Characteristics can be valuated differently for each individual article. For example, an article with the characteristic color can receive the value red and another article can receive the value blue. The system converts the characteristic values based on the conversion defined for the article. The system converts the characteristic value for selected items in the document or for the entire document. Characteristic value conversion can be carried out in documents such as sales orders, purchase orders, and so on.

processes.name: Contract-Based Revenue Recognition – IFRS
processes.overview: The scope item enables you to manage revenue recognition in accordance with IFRS 15, applying the five-step model. It forms the foundation of Universal Revenue Recognition, which integrates the Event-Based Revenue Recognition and Contract-Based Revenue Recognition functionalities. With Universal Revenue Recognition activated, in scenarios where bundles of customer projects, sales orders, or service contracts are sold, revenue contracts are automatically created from the objects deemed relevant for revenue accounting and corresponding performance obligations in each revenue contract are generated based on the items within these relevant objects. In addition, the revenue contracts generated automatically can be combined together according to the business requirements. Revenue is allocated across the performance obligations based on the standalone selling price and contractual price. As costs are posted, such as through goods issue posting, the matching revenue is recognized in real time, taking advantage of existing Event-Based Revenue Recognition capabilities. In scenarios where Contract Accounting – Contract-Based Revenue Recognition (3L3) is operational, it aids in revenue accounting for revenue contracts and performance obligations that are created based on provider contracts. Furthermore, it supports the integration with external operational systems, using an API to create and update revenue contracts.

processes.name: Cross-Plant Kanban Processes – Consumer Products
processes.overview: This scope item describes a cross-plant Kanban process in the Consumer Products industry. The Kanban method for managing material replenishment between plants is based on the actual stock situation at the receiving location. When a Kanban container is set to empty, the system triggers a stock transfer from a supplying plant. The material is staged in defined quantities and transported to the receiving plant to ensure a continuous and demand-driven material supply at the consumption location. According to the pull principle, replenishment isn't initiated by central planning, but directly by the receiving location when additional stock is required. The process is executed with predefined control cycle data to ensure that each Kanban status change automatically initiates the required logistical activities. In this stock transfer scenario, the process starts when a Kanban container is set to empty. This action automatically triggers the creation of an outbound delivery in the supplying plant. The substeps include executing picking and posting goods issue. As soon as the material arrives at the receiving plant, the Kanban container is set to full, which automatically posts the goods receipt in the system.

processes.overview: In this scenario, the goods are initially posted to the customer consignment stock and thus remain the property of the company (consignment fill-up). At regular intervals, the customer reports how many articles are sold and how many articles are in the current stock (inventory). When the inventory is performed, the batch number may be entered to do a correct material posting. A corresponding sales order is entered that documents the issue from the customer consignment, meaning that the goods are no longer the property of the company (consignment issue). Goods that are not required can be returned from the consignment stock to the central warehouse. The goods must not be defective. They are posted directly into the free stock (consignment pick-up). In some cases, goods are returned to the customer consignment stock (by its own customer or based on erroneous consumption posting) after the consignment issue has already taken place. A return order is then created (consignment return).

processes.name: Data Protection and Privacy – Data Controller and Purpose
processes.overview: With this scope item, SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition simplifies the separation of business partner master data based on legal entities (data controllers) and purposes. This approach supports privacy by design and default. Many business processes that involve personal data begin with the creation of master data. When you create and manage a business partner, you can add several types of data to that business partner. Examples include contact details, financial information, and employment history. Each type of data creates different levels of privacy risk for individuals. To manage these risks, this scope item provides a switch to a data model that lets you manage personal data according to the legal entities responsible for the data (data controllers) and the purposes for collecting and processing the data. This helps you comply with legal standards. After you centrally define data controllers and purposes and assign these to business partners, you can restrict access to business partner master data based on these assignments. This ensures that only authorized users access the personal data of business partners. You can activate these authorization checks separately for data controllers and purposes. This gives you flexibility in your implementation. You can start by separating data based on data controllers and then introduce purpose-based authorization checks if required.

processes.name: Demand-Driven Buffer Level Management
processes.overview: Demand-driven replenishment (DD) helps to plan and manage supply chains efficiently based on customer demand, rather than through traditional MRP procedures. It forms the basis for a reliable material flow by defining buffers at strategically important points and adjusting these buffers regularly. Products at all Bill-of-Material (BoM) levels are classified based on average demand, lead time, BoM usage, and variability to identify if they are relevant for demand-driven replenishment. A well-balanced buffer level is proposed for DD-relevant products to ensure that they are sufficiently stocked to meet average demand, but in low enough quantities to prevent excessive storage costs or losses due to expiry. An app helps planners manage safety stock, reorder point, and maximum stock through the buffer level proposals. To support the calculation of buffer levels, predictive material and resource planning (pMRP) can be deployed.

processes.name: Empties for Retail
processes.overview: Some retailers sell articles to which deposit-relevant packaging articles are assigned to. Consumers buy the packaging article with the main article and pay a deposit price for it. This packaging article can later be returned by the consumer and the deposit is refunded. Beverages are the most common example. In some countries or regions, the empty bottle (and potentially also the crate containing multiple bottles) are subject to deposit handling. For example, an empty bottle is sold along with the lemonade (the full article), and twelve empty bottles and an empty crate are sold together with a crate of lemonade. The article master for the full article is set up with a bill of material, reflecting the assignment of the full article to the relevant empties. The relationship of full and empty articles is carried through all supply chain processes and respective operational documents, starting with the procurement from external suppliers (purchase orders), and ending with the sale to consumer (sales in the store). In inventory management, two types of empties stock are distinguished. The tied empties stock reflects the quantities attached to the full articles, but the untied stock considers only the inventory of stand-alone empties (for example, an empty bottle returned by the consumer on its way back to the supplier). Inventory reporting considers both types of stock. From a financial perspective, tied and untied empties are typically held in different accounts.

processes.overview: SAP Excise Tax Management by Vistex for Public Cloud extends SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition by providing a cloud-native framework for excise tax compliance. The solution runs on the SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) and integrates with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for transactional, master, and financial data. Organizations can track excise-relevant goods, calculate accurate tax amounts, and generate legal reports required by authorities. The Stock Ledger Workspace allows users to validate, reprocess, and monitor excise transactions through a modern SAP Fiori user interface. processes.name: First Article Inspection – Consumer Products
processes.overview: This scope item describes a process in the consumer products industry to manage the first article inspection (FAI) and regular inspection of a raw material. As an example material, a foil is used, which becomes a viewing window bag during production. Before the foil is released to production, the material must meet the specifications negotiated with the supplier. To ensure this, a small sample quantity is ordered with the first purchase order and inspected with a special inspection plan. The Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) in the quality info record controls this, where the purchase order item is maintained. At goods receipt, the inspection lot is created with the special first article inspection plan for first check. This plan contains a general goods receipt inspection by the quality team as well as an additional inspection by a special team responsible for the print layout inspection. After results recording and the usage decision, you can monitor the result of the first article inspection in the quality info record. If the FAI is accepted, the print layout is shared with the supplier. A new purchase order with normal quantity can be created. The process continues with the goods receipt and the regular goods receipt inspection. If the FAI is rejected, the same process can be repeated with a new purchase order item and a new quality info record maintenance. This type of first article inspection requires an inspection plan structure with several operations. However, the structure of this inspection plan can be simpler in your company, as you may not need different operations and work centers, though you may need different inspection plans with the corresponding inspection plan usage.

processes.name: Freight Settlement
processes.overview: Freight costs calculated for the freight documents (freight orders and freight bookings) are to be posted in financial accounting to record such costs in accounting as accruals and to pay the carriers or freight forwarders. Once the freight documents are in a status in which the transportation has been initiated or completed, the freight costs can be posted to financial accounting. If there are errors during the posting of accruals, the freight documents can be monitored for such posting errors. The invoice received from the carrier or freight forwarder is verified against the expected costs calculated in the freight document. Depending on the number of invoicing parties involved for a freight document, multiple invoices can be received from different carriers executing the transport. For example, for an ocean freight booking, you can receive invoices from different invoicing carriers to execute different stages of the ocean booking (for example, one for the pick-up, one for the main carriage, and another one for the delivery). During invoice verification, price variances and unplanned freight costs can be captured. Freight cost allocation capabilities are used to manage freight costs that occurred during the transportation processes. The costs are posted to a material valuation in an inbound process, and to an expense account (general ledger) in an outbound process.

processes.name: Inbound Logistics for Distribution Centers
processes.overview: The purchase order is the basis for all goods receipt processing. The purchase order is communicated to the external supplier. As the goods are shipped, the supplier can optionally send the corresponding shipping documents to the recipient. These Advance Shipping Notices (ASN) can be posted up front in the system as an inbound delivery before the actual arrival of the merchandise in the distribution center (DC). Compared to the purchase order and an optional order confirmation, the ASN gives more accurate information about the expected quantities and dates, thus enhancing supply chain transparency. Part of the goods receipt articles and their quantities can be prefilled by data from the purchase order or inbound delivery. After counting, the quantities can be adjusted if needed. As a result of posting the good receipt, the inventory is adjusted accordingly and the respective financial accounts are posted. If differences are discovered later, you can make the necessary corrections, partially cancelling the goods receipt. A variant of goods receipt handling is the receiving of merchandise returned from a store to the DC.

processes.name: Internal Commissions Settlement for Sales
processes.overview: The internal commissions settlement capabilities support you in offering sales commissions as incentives to employees and paying commissions on schedule. The internal commission settlement can be based on workforce condition contracts, or you can import commission data from SAP SuccessFactors Incentive Management. The payout of commissions happens with SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll. In the first business scenario for internal commissions settlement, you use condition contracts from Condition Contract Management to enter the sales commission agreements for internal sales representatives. In a condition contract, you specify the personnel number of the commission recipient, organizational and process control parameter, the business volume selection criteria, the sales commission conditions, and the settlement calendar with settlement dates for delta accrual and final settlement. The delta accruals settlement reflects a procedure in which accruals for commissions aren't posted together with the transactional documents but subsequently in a specific settlement run. In final settlements of condition contracts, usually aligned with the salary process for employees, you perform the sales commission calculation based on business volume and commission conditions and you create the personnel settlement documents. In the second business scenario, the process starts in SAP SuccessFactors Incentive Management with the calculation of the commissions amount for the employees and continues with the import of this data to create the personnel settlement documents in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Usually, personnel settlement documents created in both processing variants are automatically released to accounting leading to postings to the corresponding accounts for commissions in Finance. Optionally, the workflow functionality can be used in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for the release of the personnel settlement documents to accounting. The commission data contained in personnel settlement documents is transferred to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and then to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll. The payroll run is executed in the payroll system. The payout to the employee is run and finally the posting on the liability account in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system is done.

processes.name: Inventory Management for Distribution Centers
processes.overview: Articles held by a retailer are known as inventory. Inventory management comprises analytical (for example, stock overview) and operational processes (for example, moving goods within a site or changing the status of the stock). In inventory management, you can keep information on the quantities and valuation of the article stock. The valuation is kept in financial accounts and is needed for legally required financial closing statements. Typically, a retailer needs both quantity and valuation information. Two main types of activities are relevant for inventory management: first, processes where articles are physically moved (goods movements), such as goods receipts, goods issues, or transfers from one storage location to another; second, processes where the status of stock is changed, such as from unrestricted use to scrapping, or from blocked quality management to unrestricted use. Both types of activities are recorded in article documents. Posting such an article document results in quantity updates, and in some cases also leads to postings to financial accounts. For example, a movement from one storage location to another leads to a quantity update of the article for the storage location but doesn't need to be reflected in financial accounting, as the value hasn't changed. Article documents also serve auditing purposes; every change in quantity or value is reported, as well as who executed it (including the link to the resulting financial posting). The stock overview displays the current stock situation on different levels (for example site group, site, or storage location) and different status (for example unrestricted use, quality inspection, or in transit).

Finally, user approvals of invoices can be done natively in the solution, or configured to work seamlessly with S4HANA, and once fully approved, these are automatically posted to the corresponding finance system for payment. processes.name: Invoice Verification for Retail
processes.overview: Once goods are procured from a supplier and placed on the company’s premises through goods receipt, the retailer (recipient) must pay the supplier for the acquired goods. The amount to be paid and the material details are provided by the supplier in the form of an invoice document. Before paying to the supplier, the retailer must verify the invoice. This scope item covers the verification of the invoice before making a payment. Before the procurement from external suppliers, the retailer carries out a logistics invoice verification. The content of invoice sent from the supplier is compared with the content of the two preceding main documents (the purchase order and the goods receipt). This process is also called three-way matching. The values of the articles and the quantities from the invoice are compared with those of the actual goods receipts. Prices and other conditions from the invoice are compared with those of the purchase order. When the values match, the invoice can be posted directly or after an optional release step. As a result, the respective financial accounts are posted to and handed over for payment. If there are discrepancies, you can decide either to accept or reject them, triggering the corresponding communication to the supplier.

processes.name: Just-In-Time Supply to Customer
processes.overview: The process starts with receiving Just-In-Time (JIT) calls from customers. JIT calls are sent via an EDI integration and contain the component details with the requirements date and time. The material planner (JIT supply) monitors and manages the JIT calls. The production planner releases production-relevant component group materials or package units for production for summarized and sequenced JIT calls respectively. The production operator then confirms the production of the components. The production supervisor reprocesses failed stocks. The shipping specialist (JIT supply) creates deliveries that reflect the status accordingly. Advanced shipping notifications are sent via EDI to the OEM. The shipping specialist and material planner can create handling units as well. After picking and posting of goods issue, the JIT call status is updated. Optionally, for summarized JIT calls, picking and post goods issue can be done in Extended Warehouse Management. After the billing is created, the JIT call is updated to completed status.

processes.overview: The process starts with receiving a Just -In- time (JIT) call from customers (see the Just-In-Time Supply to Customer (2EM) scope item). During the processing of such JIT calls, the goods are posted as consignment stock. Consignment goods are stored at the customer location but owned by suppliers. The customers are not obligated to pay for these goods until they remove it from consignment stock. As the goods are consumed, customers send JIT delivery confirmations via SOAP API with information about materials, quantity, and reference JIT calls. The delivery confirmation is matched with the existing JIT calls within the supplier system. The material planner (JIT supply) has an option to release them manually. Once the delivery confirmation is released, subsequent documents (such as customer consignment issue order and outbound delivery related to customer consignment issue order) are created and the goods issue is posted. After the billing is done, the JIT call lifecycle status is updated.

processes.name: Lot Size of One with Advanced Variant Configuration
processes.overview: This scope item focuses on a Make-to-Order scenario (Lot Size of One) that integrates with production planning and execution, procurement, inquiry, quotation, sales, and logistics execution up to invoicing and incoming and outgoing payments, covering multilevel configurable materials. The configurable material is defined as a bill of material. In this process, the storyline starts with an inquiry for a robot, proceeding to a quotation and on confirmation a sales order is created with an individual configuration. This is captured by defining the different component characteristics desired by the customers and considering the constraints and dependencies of the components. The sales price calculation is then based on the individually chosen characteristics of the components. The sales order is considered for production planning when doing the materials requirements planning (MRP). Configured subassemblies are procured externally based on the procurement proposal generated during MRP. Another configured subassembly is transferred to production plant from another plant belonging to the same company code. Special procurement indicators are used to define stock transfer locations. Stock is placed in special sales order stock at all times and serialized (as of level subassembly). By serializing stock throughout the process, this allows customers to gain transparency for items that are built in the configured finished good. The production execution for the individual robot takes place after one subassembly is procured externally (including configuration information), while another subassembly is internally produced. The finished good (robot) is subject to quality inspection at the end of production. Once production is complete, the goods are delivered to the customer and invoiced. The process finishes with posting of incoming payments from the customer as well as outgoing payments to the vendor for purchased subassemblies. processes.name: Maintenance Order Processing with SAP Field Service Management
processes.overview: This scope item describes end-to-end business scenarios that connect SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition reactive maintenance order processing with SAP Field Service Management. The reactive maintenance process lets users perform maintenance on assets when a breakdown or failure occurs. After users create and release a reactive maintenance order in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the system creates a corresponding service call in SAP Field Service Management. The system creates an activity for each operation in the maintenance order. It also replicates components as reserved materials. Users assign an activity to a technician on the planning board in SAP Field Service Management. When users release the activity, the system automatically updates the technician in the corresponding maintenance order operation in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. When users approve confirmations such as efforts, expenses, or materials in SAP Field Service Management, the system creates a confirmation in the maintenance order and automatically completes it in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

processes.overview: This scope item supports production planning for semifinished components within a Make-to-Order (MTO) environment before the receipt of incoming sales orders. This reduces the lead time of sales orders for finished goods received that are received later. Demand forecast is created for semifinished components that are represented through planned independent requirements (PIRs). Based on PIRs, Material Requirements Planning (MRP) creates a production plan for the component and explodes the bill of material structure for higher low-level codes. As a result, the demand for semifinished component production and raw material is planned. The production process is made up of the following: Conversion of planned orders to production orders, order release, confirmation of order operations with automatic backflush of components, and goods receipt posting. The scenario is completed with the receipt of an incoming sales order and either the consumption of the component part of this scope item, or by reference to the entire MTO scenario in the BJE scope item.

processes.name: Make-to-Stock – Process Manufacturing Based on Process Order
processes.overview: This scope item enables production planning in make-to-stock scenarios and quick reactions to incoming sales orders. The focus is on process manufacturing (for example, supported through process orders or batch management). The process starts with the creation of a demand forecast for finished goods represented by planned independent requirements (PIRs). Based on PIRs, Material Requirements Planning (MRP) creates a production plan for finished goods, semifinished components, and raw materials. Production planners can analyze and change the planned-order-based production plan manually. Raw material demand leads to purchase requisitions that trigger alternative procurement scenarios referenced in this scope item. The production process itself is entirely covered via conversion of planned into process orders, order release, direct material issue or backflush, confirmation of operations, and goods receipt posting. Order-based target and actual costs are created, ensuring fully integrated material and value streams. Regulated industries are also supported with process order approval based on approved master data (master recipe, BOM, and so on).

processes.name: Make-to-Stock Production – Repetitive Manufacturing
processes.overview: Repetitive Manufacturing is commonly used when a production process meets the following criteria: This scenario begins with Planned Independent Requirements (PIR), which are used to perform demand management functions. Material Requirements Planning (MRP) generates planned orders for the materials to be produced. By using the planning table, the production of materials and capacity on the production lines can be planned. Confirming Repetitive Manufacturing triggers multiple activities, such as finished product goods receipt, backflushing of component materials, posting costs to cost collectors, and creating material and journal entries. In Repetitive Manufacturing, the master plan is represented by the planning table, which is a tool for operative planning and is used to plan production quantities. In a repetitive manufacturing environment, planning and control are usually performed on a period and quantity basis. The planning table's layout has been designed to support this requirement and is also based on periods to provide a clear, easy-to-interpret overview of materials and production lines. The planning table is the Production Planner's or MRP Controller's most important tool for planning production quantities. At a glance, they can check production quantities, monitor the available capacity of the production lines, and check the availability of the products produced on each line. Production quantities can be directly entered and changed in the planning table. 'Nonassigned' production quantities can be assigned to the production lines, or production quantities can be reassigned to alternative production lines. The planning table can be used for planning with planned orders and production orders. The only prerequisite is that a valid production version must be created in the material master record.

processes.name: Material Replenishment with Kanban – External Procurement
processes.overview: The Kanban method for controlling production and material flow is based on the actual stock quantity in production. Material that is required on a regular basis is continually provided in small quantities into production. With Kanban, instead of being pushed through production by higher-level planning, materials are called from the supply source by production at the manufacturing level where they are needed (pull principle). Replenishment or production of a material is only triggered when a higher production level requires the material. This replenishment is triggered directly in production using previously maintained master data. Kanban replenishment is commonly used in – but not restricted to – repetitive manufacturing environments when a production process requires that the same or similar products are produced over a certain period at a certain rate per period. The products produced always follow the same sequence through the machines and work centers in production. Routings tend to be simple and do not vary much.

This is for various reasons, such as one-off articles, stock reduction in distribution centers, special offer from supplier, end-of-season clearance, and so on. The push scenario complements the pull scenario realized via consumption-based replenishment. For more information, see the Replenishment Planning for Stores (3I7) scope item . The planning tool for the push scenario is the so-called allocation table. First, the user enters relevant articles, the quantities to be distributed, store groups, and various dates (order date, receiving dates for stores and distributions centers, and optionally, delivery phases). One of several available types of merchandise distribution is then selected, including: The quantities for each receiving store are calculated based on different available options (such as ratios or strategies). Once the planning is finalized, the respective orders can be created automatically; the orders are handed over to operational procurement for execution.

processes.name: Merchandise Distribution and Collective Purchase Order
processes.overview: Through collective purchase order processing, you can consolidate procurement for stores for efficient processing by an external supplier. Merchandise distribution manages the planned quantities for the stores, makes necessary adjustments, and efficiently executes logistics processes in the distribution center. This scope item describes merchandise procurement through a pull process. First, you determine the demand for the stores and create the resulting documents as described in the scope item Replenishment Planning for Stores (3I7). If the supply source is a distribution center, you can combine the demand from stores into a collective purchase order for the distribution center at the external supplier. You can create collective purchase orders either online or by scheduling a batch job run in the background. At the same time, the information for the merchandise distribution is created, and the quantities for the stores along with further data are being recorded. After receiving the goods in the distribution center, you can adjust the quantities for the stores if the received quantities differ from those in the purchase order. You can adjust the merchandise distribution quantities either through a merchandise distribution monitor or in the background through a batch run. After the adjustment, the system creates and processes outbound deliveries for pickup and posts the goods issue. Finally, the stores receive the merchandise. In case of automatic adjustment, the quantities are distributed to the stores and outbound deliveries are generated automatically at the time of goods receipt at distribution center.

processes.name: Nonconformance Management
processes.overview: This scope item describes the management of defects and nonconformances. The quality technician creates a defect record and if necessary, adds a picture that documents the defect. The quality engineer further processes the defect record by documenting or defining immediate, corrective, and preventive actions. The quality technician executes the defined actions and confirms processing by setting a respective status. After defect resolution, the quality engineer closes the defect record. In addition to general defect category, a new defect category is introduced which can be used to handle defects that occur during production. That is, the assignment of production order, material, plant, and defective quantity has been enabled. Furthermore, the quality engineer monitors and analyzes defect records from various sources (for example, defects detected during quality inspection or manually created defects) and deduces common preventive actions. If necessary, the quality technician creates additional, manual inspection lots for the available inspection origins to perform additional quality inspections. After inspection results are captured, the quality engineer makes a usage decision to close the manual inspection process.

processes.name: Omnichannel Order Fulfillment for Retail
processes.overview: In today’s retail environment, retailers must account for the situation where a consumer buys merchandise online and picks it up in a store. This benefits both the consumer and the retailer. For consumers, it eliminates the risk of missed deliveries, theft of delivered items, and unnecessary shipping charges. For retailers, it's more cost-effective than home delivery and opens up opportunities for additional sales once the consumer is in the store. This scope item describes the fulfillment of orders placed online by consumers to be picked up in the stores. Consumers can order articles using e-commerce and pick them up at a store of their choice. This is known as buy online, pick-up in store (BOPIS) or Click-and-Collect. Two main process steps are supported: First, the process of picking the articles from the sales floor, and second, the handover of the merchandise to the consumers. To cater for requirements of different retailer’s formats, processes can be set up flexibly (for example, small fashion boutique vs. grocery retailer). A process variant is the Click-and-Reserve, where the merchandise isn't paid using e-commerce channels, but after handover in the store.

processes.overview: The cycle counting method is a special physical inventory procedure where inventory is counted at regular intervals within a fiscal year. In general, it starts with classification of materials based on ABC analysis or at the user's discretion. Additional counting intervals are set based on classification of materials. The physical stocks are compared and realized for the given materials in the system. Any discrepancies in the system quantities and physical count are reviewed. The inventory may be recounted until final counts are accepted and inventory differences are posted.

processes.name: Planning and Production in Other Plant – Consumer Products
processes.overview: This scope item describes a cross-plant production planning and execution process tailored for the Consumer Products Industry. The process involves two plants: Plant 1 serves as the planning and packaging plant using production orders, while Plant 2 produces semifinished materials using process manufacturing. The process begins with creating a demand forecast for the finished goods, represented by Planned Independent Requirements (PIRs) in Plant 1. Based on these PIRs, Material Requirements Planning (MRP) generates a production plan for finished goods and explodes the entire bill of material structure across both plants. As a result, the demand for semifinished component production, packaging, and raw materials is planned in both plants, depending on the BOM structure. The production process starts by converting a planned order to a process order or directly creating a process order in Plant 2. Subsequently, goods issue of components, confirmation of production, and goods receipt of the semifinished goods are executed. Plant 1 hosts all major packaging materials, including those relevant for Plant 2. The withdrawal via pick list is executed cross-plant: Cartons are posted directly in Plant 1, even though Plant 2 consumes the material, while Plant 2 picks and posts other components. Moreover, the goods receipt of the semifinished material is posted directly in Plant 1, even though production takes place in Plant 2, eliminating the need for a separate stock transfer process. Plant 1 stores the semifinished material until a customer places an order for the finished material, triggering the packaging process. The MRP run creates convertible planned orders according to customer requirements. The packaging process begins with converting these planned orders to production orders. After production and goods receipt of the finished material in the unrestricted stock, the system can deliver the sales order and initiate the billing process.

With the supply of the finished material, the goods receipt is created. The consumption of the sent components is recorded upon the receipt of the value-added finished material. The production process itself covers the conversion of planned orders into production orders, order release, material staging and picking, confirmation of order operations, and goods receipt posting. Raw materials within production can be replenished by Kanban procurement. A semifinished good is produced via a repetitive manufacturing scenario integrated with in-process inspection and Kanban. Order-based target and actual cost is created, ensuring fully integrated material and value streams. For an additional subassembly, repetitive manufacturing is executed. The process continues with the creation of a sales order, checking the legal compliance with international trade regulations, performing the delivery with picking and quality inspection at goods issue, invoicing, ending with the clearing after incoming payment. processes.name: Produce to Sell – Process Industry – Consumer Products
processes.overview: This document describes an integrated end-to-end scenario for the consumer products industry that combines batch-managed production in the process industry, quality assurance through first article inspections, and commercial settlement within a customer hierarchy using condition contracts. For this, three scope items are combined: The process starts with requirement planning for finished goods using PIRs. You use Material Requirements Planning (MRP) to create a plan by exploding the BOM and generating requirements to produce semifinished and finished products, as well as purchasing requirements for externally procured components. Incoming quality assurance is integrated via first article inspection for purchased materials. After you create a purchase order and post the goods receipt, inspection plans are referenced to record inspection results and make a usage decision. If first article inspection is accepted, subsequent purchase orders follow a regular goods receipt inspection. If the first article is rejected, a new purchase order with first article inspection is created. Optional overviews before and after a goods receipt inspection for quality technician and quality engineer support transparency without being mandatory for the core flow. For two-stage batch derivation, the production process starts by executing a process order for the semifinished material, followed by goods issue of batch-managed components, production confirmation, and goods receipt. The final processing and packaging level is started with a process order for the finished product followed by the confirmation of component consumption, production times, and goods receipt of the finished product. Each goods receipt triggers a batch derivation and updates batch attributes according to the configured strategy. The results can be verified in the derivation monitor, with end-to-end traceability checks available in the Batch Information Cockpit (top-down and bottom-up). Manual derivation is possible but not included in this scope. The stock produced is used to fulfill demand for the sale from stock. After sales order processing via order creation, delivery, and billing, the business completion is done via condition contract management within the customer hierarchy: condition contract creation, business volume determination based on executed sales, execution of final settlement, and verification of settlement documents to confirm the correct calculation and posting of rewards and rebates.

processes.name: Quality Management for Complaints Against Suppliers
processes.overview: This scope item describes the management of complaints against suppliers, for example, after delivery of a product. Leveraging quality notifications, the quality engineer captures all complaint-related information including the observed defects. The quality engineer enters immediate actions for documentation purposes and requests a root cause analysis from the supplier. Furthermore, the quality engineer can keep a record of his communication with the supplier. Leveraging the new nonconformance management business object “Complaint against Supplier”, the quality engineer records the complaint basic data, maintains the involved roles, assigns existing defects, and initiates logistical follow-up actions such as the creation of a returns purchase order — directly within the process flow. The system facilitates seamless communication with the supplier by generating a detailed complaint report to request formal feedback. Finally, the quality engineer reviews the findings, monitors the status of the complaint, and completes the process, ensuring full transparency from initial defect identification to final resolution. The quality engineer defines tasks either globally at notification level or per defect. The quality engineer assigns one processor to each task. The task is processed, and task processors give feedback per task. After having received the supplier's root cause analysis, identified root causes can be assigned to each defect. Finally, the quality engineer reviews each task and closes the notification.

processes.name: Quality Management in Discrete Manufacturing – Consumer Products
processes.overview: This scope item outlines a Consumer Products Industry-flavored production process that fully integrates Quality Management into discrete Manufacturing. It operates as a Make-to-stock scenario for batch-managed goods, incorporating QM for In-Process Control and early goods receipt inspection. The Consumer Industry process involves a two-stage production process for coffee displays. The first stage covers the roasting and packaging of medium respective dark roasted beans, considering the fixed capacity of the roasting drums. During the roasting, cooling and packaging steps, quality inspection continuously monitors the process. During roasting, the temperature, browning of the beans and other parameters are constantly checked by QM until all parameters are fulfilled. Moreover, the early goods receipt inspection functionality handles the End-Product Control of unpacked, semifinished products as flexibly as possible. This means users can start end-product control during the production process or after receiving goods into quality stock. The second stage involves a display packaging process where two different semifinished products, such as bags of medium and dark roasted coffee beans, are packed into a display carton. In this step, a quality inspection is set up after receiving goods from production into quality inspection stock. The process begins with creating a demand forecast for finished goods, represented by Planned Independent Requirements (PIRs). You can create these PIRs manually or by using an upload file. Based on the PIRs, Material Requirements Planning (MRP) generates a production plan for finished goods and breaks down the entire bill of material structure. This results in the planning of semifinished component production and raw material demands. Production planners can analyze and manually adjust the planned orders according to the production plan. Raw material demands lead to purchase requisitions, which trigger alternative procurement scenarios referenced in this scope item. The production process includes converting planned orders to production orders, order release, material staging and picking, confirming order operations or complete orders, and posting goods receipts. Order-based targets and actual costs are created to ensure fully integrated material and value streams.

processes.name: Reactive Maintenance
processes.overview: The reactive maintenance process has nine steps from the creation of a maintenance notification to its completion. Reactive maintenance process allows you to perform maintenance of an asset whenever a breakdown or a failure occurs. First, you create a maintenance notification (Initiation). Next, the maintenance notification is screened and accepted (Screening). The maintenance notification is converted into a maintenance order. During this phase, the required resources for processing the order are also planned (Planning). The maintenance order is then approved for execution (Approval). Next, the maintenance order is prepared for execution. Various requirements such as stock, nonstock material, purchase requisition, and capacity are reviewed (Preparation). After this, the maintenance order is scheduled for execution (Scheduling). The maintenance order is then executed to repair the malfunction (Execution). Activities such as failure data recording and other post-work activities are performed (Post Execution). Finally, the maintenance order is reviewed and is technically completed (Completion). For minor or emergency work, not all steps need to be executed. When you select the notification processing context in the Manage Maintenance Notification app, you also decide the variation of the reactive maintenance process (minor or emergency). To enable safety instructions, you need to activate the Health and Safety Management (54A) scope item.

processes.name: Replenishment Planning for Distribution Centers
processes.overview: The goal of the replenishment process for distribution centers is to calculate optimal dates and quantities for the procurements of reorderable articles from suppliers to best meet demand. First, demand is determined by executing forecasting algorithms on historical consumption data, considering various factors (such as seasonality) to feed into consumption-based planning. Alternatively, demand can be expressed by planned independent requirements (PIR). Next, material requirements planning (MRP) is executed to calculate the optimal quantities and dates for the procurement. The replenishment calculation considers demand, current stock situation, already planned goods receipts, and supplier parameters. MRP can be controlled via different MRP types (for example, time phased planning), for which it's possible to specify certain weekdays for ordering and delivery. The result of the MRP execution is then handed over to the operational procurement via purchase requisitions.

In an optional preliminary step to the replenishment run, demand can be determined by executing forecasting algorithms on historical consumption data, considering various factors (such as seasonality). Alternatively, you can create planned independent requirements (PIRs) to determine demand. Replenishment is executed to calculate the optimal quantities and dates for procurement, considering among others, forecast demand or PIRs, the current stock situation, and already planned goods receipts. Additionally, a manually (for example based on shelf size and presentation stock) or automatically determined target stock can be considered. Replenishment triggers the creation of purchase requisitions for the determined quantities and dates.

processes.name: Sales Price Valuation for Retail
processes.overview: Stock valuation for all articles carried in stores and distribution centers is mandatory, as it serves as foundation for balance sheet accounting and legally required financial closing statements. This cost-based stock valuation comes in two flavors: moving average cost (determined by averaging purchase cost in goods receipts) or standard prices (which are fixed during a validity period). In addition to valuation at cost, many retailers require that valuation at expected sales prices is carried in parallel. This allows retailers to always have up-to-date margin information at hand as a basis for crucial merchandising decisions, such as how to build their assortments. Furthermore, having valuation at cost and sales prices in tandem is required for most planning and reporting activities. Valuation at sales prices can be used for both stores and distribution centers. Sales price values are determined for all article movements (for example goods receipts or goods issues), and stored in the respective article documents. There are two basic reasons for sales price revaluations of stock: In both scenarios, sales price revaluation documents are created to support reporting and auditing.

processes.name: SAP EWM Integration – Batch Management
processes.overview: This scope item describes the basic integration of batches in the goods receipt process with SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM). It allows you to create batches in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and in the SAP EWM system as required. When creating batches in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the batch master record is distributed to the EWM system. During the creation of a purchase order, the business user can enter the batch number for each purchase order item. Once a purchase order is available, an inbound delivery is created and replicated to the SAP EWM system. The batch number is distributed as part of the delivery item. If you don't assign a specific batch in the purchase order / inbound delivery, you can search for a fitting batch or create a new one in SAP EWM. In this case, the batch data is transferred to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system.

processes.name: SAP EWM Integration – Delivery-Based Production Integration
processes.overview: In this scope item, you manage the staging and consumption of components from the warehouse to production and the receiving and storage of finished products from production into the warehouse. You trigger material staging that leads to the creation of an outbound delivery that is replicated to SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM). The corresponding outbound delivery order (ODO) in SAP EWM serves as the main document for material staging. A warehouse clerk creates warehouse tasks for staging with reference to the ODO. The warehouse worker moves the goods to the production supply area and confirms the warehouse tasks. A goods issue is automatically posted by the system. The stock is transferred from the EWM-managed to the production storage location and is now available for consumption. After the production process is finished, the generation of expected goods receipts (EGR) documents initiates the receiving of the finished goods from production into the warehouse.

processes.name: SAP EWM Integration – Inbound Processing from Supplier
processes.overview: This scope item enables you to order goods from suppliers and to perform the putaway in your warehouse. The process begins with the creation of a purchase order and an inbound delivery in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. If the delivery is relevant to processing in SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM), the inbound delivery document is replicated to the SAP EWM system, where it generates an inbound delivery notification that in turn leads to an inbound delivery. Alternatively, the warehouse can be informed about incoming goods by using an expected goods receipt (EGR) document. You can transfer the expected goods receipt information to the SAP EWM system in one of two ways: pull data from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition from within SAP EWM, or push the data from SAP S/4HANA Cloud to SAP EWM. The EGR document contains data for a purchase order and enables you to create an inbound delivery in SAP EWM that is replicated to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

processes.name: SAP EWM Integration – Outbound Processing to Customer
processes.overview: In this process, you ship ordered goods to external customers using SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition integrated to SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM). This process starts with the creation of a sales order and an outbound delivery. The outbound delivery is replicated to the SAP EWM, where an outbound delivery order is created. This document serves as the starting point for the outbound processing within the warehouse. Warehouse tasks are created with reference to the outbound delivery order and the physical process for picking is executed. During the creation of warehouse tasks, the system determines the location for picking the stock and allocates the stock to the warehouse task. At the end of the process, the goods issue is posted. The goods issue information is transferred from SAP EWM to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. Subsequent process steps such as billing can be executed accordingly.

processes.name: SAP EWM Integration – Stock Transport Orders
processes.overview: Using stock transport orders, you can execute a stock transfer process from one plant to another within the same company code. The process starts with the creation of a stock transport order. A warehouse clerk at the shipping plant monitors the materials due for shipment and creates deliveries as required. Once a delivery is created, the system replicates it to the SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) system, where an outbound delivery order is created. Warehouse tasks are created with reference to the outbound delivery order and the physical process for picking is executed. After the goods issue is posted in the SAP EWM system and sent back to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, an inbound delivery is created and replicated to SAP EWM automatically. This document serves as the starting point for the inbound process in the receiving plant.

processes.name: SAP Maintenance Assistant
processes.overview: This scope item enables a maintenance technician to improve workplace safety, optimize asset life, and ensure reliability. It also helps to streamline processes by eliminating paperwork. The mobile app accesses asset management in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and empowers the workforce to inspect, maintain, and repair assets in the field from their mobile devices. In SAP Maintenance Assistant, the Field Service Technician persona empowers technicians to deliver efficient and reliable service. It streamlines task execution, optimizes resource utilization, and improves the technician's work experience. This new persona enables technicians to access service orders, update service tasks, capture and update critical data, and collaborate on their mobile devices. SAP Maintenance Assistant also supports the SAP S/4HANA Service Quotation feature. Users can create service quotations and service quotation items from the mobile application. Integration with SAP Field Service Management (FSM) for dispatching and planning helps to reduce manual processes and enhance field productivity and operational efficiency. With this release, SAP Maintenance Assistant supports FSM integration with the Maintenance Technician persona. The SmartForms feature is now supported for both Maintenance Technician and Field Service Technician personas.

processes.name: Seasons for Retail
processes.overview: Season management forms an important aspect in the product lifecycle for the retail and fashion industry. Retail production is either predetermined or varies according to the manufacturing season. To ensure that the production life cycles are aligned with the demand, the concept of seasons as a temporal unit is used as a base for the production schedule.​ This scope item describes how to set up the season data and assign your defined seasons to products. It explains how the season data is processed for various documents individually. In the Order-to-Cash process, this scope item starts with a customer order. Season data is assigned to products at a sales order item level. Subsequently, the season data is transferred to the follow-on documents. In the Procure-to-Pay process, this scope item starts with a purchase order. Season data is assigned to products at a purchase order item level. Subsequently, the season data is transferred to the follow-on documents. In the Stock Transfer distribution process, this scope item starts with a stock transport order. Season data is assigned to products at a stock transport order item level. Subsequently, the season data is transferred to the follow-on documents. In the Advanced Intercompany process, season data from the original document is transferred to the follow-on documents. The season information copied to the follow-on documents cannot be changed in those documents. In the Returns process, the season information is copied from the original document to the returns document. In retail, a season belongs to a season year and can be associated with collections. Collections can in turn be assigned to themes. Each of these entities (season, collection, theme) has a validity period. The existence of these features helps to further classify the offering for a season, apart from providing a concept for each segment of product offering. The key attributes in product master for season functionality are season year, season, collection, theme. Season A season is a reporting period in which a special assortment limited to a specific period is merchandised and maintained in a certain way in the information system (for example, Summer season, Christmas season, Easter season, Winter season). Seasons are crucial for the fashion planning of product design and merchandising. Collection Collections are a selection of outfits that designers assemble for the upcoming season. They reflect trends, colors, cuts, and proportions. Theme Themes are based on collections in the season hierarchy, and the designers represent a theme that matches them. For example, a period in history, a foreign place, a range of colors, types of fabrics, and so on. An entity in the hierarchy is dependent on the higher-level entity. For example, a collection must be associated with a season and, likewise, a theme with a collection. Therefore, a collection or a theme can't be defined as a standalone entity in the above hierarchy. Also, a season can't be created without a season year. The timeframe is defined as an elementary attribute in the entities that indicates its applicability in a year (timeframe). You can view the hierarchy from the user menu and define a time period on one of the three levels. A sales period, purchasing period or stock transfer period defines the timeframe within which this entity (season, collection, or theme) is maintained to be valid for the corresponding application documents.

processes.name: Segmentation for Retail
processes.overview: In today’s increasingly customer-driven market, products must often be differentiated based on specific requirements such as quality levels, sourcing origins, or distribution strategies. Segmentation enables companies to logically categorize demand, inventory, and supply, supporting tailored planning, sourcing, and fulfillment processes. At its core, segmentation organizes products and their associated requirements or stock into logical groups based on defined business criteria. These criteria may include product quality, region of origin, market channel, or other relevant characteristics. Consider a retailer selling the same product across multiple sales channels - eCommerce, retail stores, and wholesale partners. Each channel carries distinct requirements. Through segmentation, the product can be logically divided into channel-specific segments. Incoming sales orders are automatically assigned to the appropriate demand segment based on the sales channel, while inventory is allocated and managed within corresponding stock segments. This ensures that goods designated for eCommerce, retail, or wholesale are planned, sourced, and consumed in alignment with their respective demand. By precisely matching demand segments with stock segments, segmentation provides end-to-end visibility and control ensuring that supply consistently meets the right market demand across the entire logistics chain.

processes.name: Self-Billing
processes.overview: In many sell-from-stock processes (for example, the Sell from Stock (BD9) and Sales Scheduling Agreements (3NR) scope items), the financial settlement is handled with a self-billing process with the customer. Instead of issuing an invoice to the customer, the supplier receives self-billing information from the customer, containing the reference document number, received quantity, and value to be credited to the supplier (as well as other information). This scope item focuses on the sales-related supplier's side of the self-billing processes. The supplier validates the self-billing message received from the customer and simulates results. If there are differences, credit and debit memos are created respectively to settle the account. If the differences exceed the defined tolerances, credit and debit memos are created to show the open amounts. The existing invoices and accounting documents are updated with the transferred self-billing reference number. This ensures that the financial settlement can be automated once payment advice from the customer is received. In Self-Billing with Invoice Creation, an initial invoice does not exist. Instead, it is simulated and created. To use the processes covered by this scope item, activate the scope item and integrate your SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system with SAP Self-Billing Cockpit. SAP Self-Billing Cockpit is available as a licensed product through the SAP Store. You can find it by searching for SAP Self-Billing Cockpit in the store. You can find additional information about the product and its features on the SAP Help Portal on the SAP Self-Billing Cockpit product page.

processes.name: Sell from Stock – Consumer Products
processes.overview: The process described in this scope item is a sales process for Consumer Products industry flavored products with seamless integration to the production process described in the Quality Management in Discrete Manufacturing – Consumer Products (5HK) scope item. The process starts with the creation of customer standard sales orders. A pricing condition may become relevant via the customer hierarchy. When the inventory is decided, the shipping specialist releases the inventory. The inventory is shipped to the customer, and the actual recording of the physical quantity is recorded. When the goods issue is posted, cost of goods sold is recorded in Financial Accounting. Once goods are delivered and the proof of delivery (POD) is confirmed by the ship-to-party, you can invoice the delivery. When the invoices are created, an invoice list is created for the central payer for both customers. An EDI invoice message is sent to the buyer when the billing document is saved. In addition, this scope item allows you to use valuated stock in transit (VSIT) as described in TRM – Accounting (Stock) (5QM). After the goods issue is posted to an outbound delivery, the stock is transferred into VSIT. With the transfer of control of the delivered goods to the customer (for example, based on incoterms and transportation management), the goods issue from VSIT to the customer is posted. At this point in time, revenue and COGS can be recognized.

processes.name: Sell from Stock
processes.overview: Sell-from-Stock provides a streamlined approach to order fulfillment. The Sell-from-Stock process is designed to efficiently manage and track the sales and shipment of existing inventory. It expedites order fulfillment, accurately recognizes revenue, and maintains precise financial accounting. The process begins with the creation of a customer and a standard sales order, tailored to the specific customer and their requirements. Upon completion of order picking, the shipping specialist updates the inventory to reflect the outgoing stock. This inventory relief step documents the precise quantity of goods being shipped to the customer. With the posting of the goods issue, revenue is formally recognized, and the cost of goods sold is recorded in the financial accounting system. Once the goods are delivered, the delivery can be invoiced. For preliminary alignment with customers, an optional preliminary billing document can be generated from the billing due list items. This allows for any necessary adjustments before the final billing documents, which customers are expected to settle, are created. For more information on bundling functionality relevant to IFRS 15, see SAP Note 2524569.

processes.name: Sites for Retail
processes.overview: This scope item describes how location master data can be maintained. In Retail, a location is typically referred to as a site and comes in one of two variations: store or distribution center. A store serves the main purpose of presenting and selling merchandise to consumers. To enable this, additional planning and operational processes are needed, for example goods receipt and physical inventory counting. The task of a distribution center is handling the transfer of merchandise from external suppliers to stores along the supply chain as efficiently as possible. Parameters to be considered include, cost for procurement, transportation, and storing, as well as stock level agreements for stores, among others. Depending on the detailed needs of a retailer, site-related processes need to be configured. The solution described in this scope item provides an easy way to maintain respective site data. Like other organizational data, sites are maintained using SAP Central Business Configuration. For ease of maintenance purposes, a defaulting mechanism prefills many parameters, so they don't need to be maintained by the user. Having consistent and high-quality site master data is crucial for ensuring reliable and smooth operation. SAP supports this by providing a quality assurance environment for testing and by ensuring consistent data replication to the productive environment.

processes.name: Stock Transfer with Delivery
processes.overview: The stock transfer process begins with a requirement to transfer material from one plant to another within the same company code. This request, in the form of a stock transfer requisition, may be created in the procuring plant automatically by MRP or manually by a buyer. The material master must exist in both the procuring (receiving) plant and the providing (shipping) plant. Stock transfer purchase orders are not subject to approval like other purchase orders. A buyer converts the stock transfer purchase requisition to a stock transfer purchase order. A warehouse clerk at the shipping plant monitors the materials due to be shipped and creates deliveries as required. A warehouse clerk gathers the materials and confirms the picked quantities. Once the delivery is complete, the delivery quantities are issued, and the goods are shipped, ending the process for the shipping plant. Goods are received at the receiving plant referencing to the stock transfer order.

The stock transfer without delivery can be performed in two different ways. A one-step transfer posting at the issuing plant moves the stock immediately from the issuing plant to the receiving plant. This is useful if the distance between the two plants is short and there is no need for stock-in-transit stock overview. A buyer at the receiving plant requests material with a stock transport order. This is useful if the issuing plant needs a formal request to send material to the receiving plant or the distance between the two plants is longer. There are no master data requirements beyond the material master to support the stock transfer process. The material master must exist in both the procuring (receiving) plant and the providing (issuing) plant. Also, stock transfer purchase orders are not subject to approval like other purchase orders.
