processes.overview: This business process describes a subcontracting process in the Consumer Products industry, using Subcontracting MRP Areas for disposition and Quality Inspection during goods receipt from subcontractor. It outlines a typical display packaging process executed by a subcontractor with the provision of components. Workflow functionalities are optional. The process begins with creating demand forecast for finished subcontracting materials, represented by Planned Independent Requirements (PIRs). You can enter these PIRs manually or upload them via a load file. Based on PIRs, Material Requirements Planning creates a purchasing plan for the finished materials and explodes the Bill of Materials structure for the component, which will be provided to the subcontractor. As a result, finished and packaging material demands are planned, leading to planned orders or purchase requisitions that trigger alternative procurement or production scenarios (not part of this business process). The display packaging can either be done in house (via production order – not part of the scenario) or sent to a subcontractor, for example, due to machine breakdown or limited capacity. The MRP run creates planned orders that can be converted to a production order (not part of this scenario) or to a purchase requisition. The purchase requisition is converted into a subcontract purchase order. As an alternative, the purchase order can be created manually by a requestor. The purchase order is subject to approval based on predefined parameters before being issued to the subcontractor. The system creates the outbound delivery, and the materials are picked and shipped to the subcontractor. The picking process transfers the components to the subcontracting MRP Area, indicating that the company still owns the components, but they are now at the subcontractor site. The consumption of the sent components from the subcontracting MRP Area is recorded upon the receipt of the value-added finished material. When you supply the finished material, the goods receipt is created. Subsequently, the invoicing process is triggered. As a process variant, inbound deliveries can be created to be able to monitor the delivery date. In that case, the goods receipt will be executed with relation to the inbound delivery and not to the purchase order. The components sent to the subcontractor and the subcontracted material are batch-managed. This might cause difficulties with the batch confirmation of the installed components, especially when producing the subcontracted material consumes several components. The subcontractor, who receives the component batches, can't always guarantee which component batch was consumed in which subcontracted material batch. This can be due to organizational, personnel, or cost reasons. To ensure traceability, the component batches are partially anonymized before they are sent to the subcontractor. This means that several component batches of a product are combined into one anonymous delivery batch by transferring the batch to batch of the component. It is easier for the subcontractor to report back the delivery batch of the components that has been included in a subcontracted material batch. When the goods receipt is posted for the subcontracted finished good, the components are automatically posted and the component stock at the subcontractor is decreased. The finished material is posted to quality inspection stock and an inspection lot is created based on an inspection plan. The quality technician records the inspection results. Based on these results, the quality engineer makes a usage decision, such as accepting or rejecting the material, or posting the material to unrestricted or blocked stock. If the results are rejected, a defect is automatically recorded. If the components and the display are batch-managed, there can be difficulties with the batch confirmation of the installed components, especially when several components are installed in a display. If the display consists of several components and their component batches and the subcontractor has been sent several component batches, they cannot always guarantee that they can record which component batch was installed in which display batch. This can be due to organizational, personnel, or cost reasons. To ensure traceability, the component batches are partially anonymized before they are sent to the subcontractor. This means that several component batches of a product are combined into one delivery batch. It is easier for the subcontractor to report back the delivery batch of the components that have been included in a display batch. The component batch is made anonymous as a delivery batch by transferring the batch to batch of the component.

processes.name: Supplier Consignment for Retail
processes.overview: In the consignment process, the supplier retains the complete (legal) ownership of the merchandise until the retailer sells it to a customer (buyer). From a financial perspective, the inventory is kept in the supplier account, and the retailer has non-valuated stocks in distribution centers and stores. For the retailer, an advantage of the consignment process is the reduced risk due to no capital tie up for the respective products. Additionally, the supplier can address customer's requirements without the need for its own sales force and marketing activities. During article master maintenance, you can decide if supplier consignment is relevant for each site.​ It's essential that the consignment stock category is preserved in all goods movements. Consignment stock can be transferred from distribution center to stores, and more often, goods in consignment stock can be transferred across sites as necessary. In the point-of-sale (POS) inbound processing, the stock category is determined and the consignment inventory is adjusted. For the customer order-based sales process at store and distribution center, goods issues can be posted from the consignment stock. All variations of return processes are supported – from store to the external supplier directly, or in two-steps process, which is from store to distribution center and then from distribution center to the supplier. In the stock overview, you can view if the inventory is company-owned by the retailer or consigned by a supplier. Concerning the settlement, the supplier doesn't issue the invoice directly to the retailer after the merchandise arrives at the premises of the retailer. The retailer is liable to pay the supplier only when the stock is consumed. Thus, a retailer triggers a settlement through different types of movements, for example, from POS sales, from sales orders, or from other stock adjustments.

processes.name: Supply Chain Automation with SAP Business Network
processes.overview: This scope item handles several supply chain processes as an integrated end-to-end solution. It includes SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. Subcontracting Subcontract purchase requisitions are generated either through the material requirements planning (MRP) process or manually by requestors. These requisitions are then converted into subcontract purchase orders. Purchase orders require approval based on predefined parameters before they're issued to subcontractors. Once approved, outbound deliveries are created, and goods (e.g. components and/ or raw materials) are picked and shipped to subcontractors. After the delivery of the finished materials, goods receipts are created. The consumption of sent the previously provided components is recorded when the value-added finished materials are received. This process subsequently initiates invoicing. The integrated Subcontracting processes focuses on externally produced materials (make-to-stock). Scheduling Agreements Scheduling agreements are long-term contracts with suppliers for the supply of materials under predetermined conditions. These conditions are valid for a specific period and a defined total purchase quantity. You can use scheduling agreements either with release documentation. Customizing controls this through an indicator when you define the document type for scheduling agreements. For agreements with release documentation, use the LPA document type. SA schedule lines are created with reference to a purchase scheduling agreement either through the material requirements planning process (MRP) or manually by requesters. Once the SA release has been carried out, an SA delivery schedule (forecast/JIT) is issued and communicated to the supplier. Based on the SA delivery schedule, the supplier delivers the requested goods and notifies about the upcoming delivery by sending an ASN. After the ASN has been converted into an inbound delivery, the goods receipt is posted, and the logistics invoice verification is carried out. Multi-Tier Collaboration Multi-Tier Collaboration lets you work with multiple trading partners across various processes, systems, and geographies in real time. It enhances transparency by sharing purchase orders, order confirmations, and advance ship notifications with multiple suppliers. This feature allows supply chain partners to access copies of orders, confirmations, and ship notices, with financial fields masked. They can also create component receipts upon receiving shipments. OEM buyers can manage their copy documents and view component shipments and receipts from tiered suppliers. Advanced Packaging with Handling Units Customers need standardized packaging for the materials and products they order and receive from suppliers. Without support for Handling Units during the creation of advanced shipping notifications, materials may be packed arbitrarily. This makes it challenging for customers to streamline their receiving and put-away processes. In this scenario, the replication of packaging instructions as well as the creation of ASNs with packaging data (specified in the replicated PI) is described.

processes.name: Tank Trailer Filling with Residuals
processes.overview: The process starts with creation of a filling process order based on an internal or external requirement. As a prerequisite, the tank trailer with a dedicated container ID should be weighed and the existing residual quantity should be posted to a separate residual storage location. This residual stock is considered during the subsequent filling process for the same container ID. Using container ID as a reference batch characteristic, the batch and quantity of residual stock for the specific container ID is determined for the process order using batch determination. The net quantity of manufactured product to be filled into the tank trailer is calculated by deducting the residual material that was already present in the tank from the total filling order quantity. A simple material quantity calculation formula is used for this purpose. The appropriate batches are selected using batch determination. The filling process order is executed to complete the tank trailer filling process.

processes.name: Value-Added Services for Retail
processes.overview: Customers often request price labels, custom packaging, or other special services for their orders, which must be completed before delivery. These value-added services (VAS) are essential in retail, especially to meet specific customer expectations. Fulfilling VAS typically requires additional products (materials), expertise, or personnel, and may therefore incur a surcharge. For example, a customer may order slacks and skirts and request that they be packed separately. Due to the delicate nature of the skirts, the customer specifies that no more than ten be packed per carton. In the system, this packing requirement can be defined as a service type, along with the maximum quantity per carton. A surcharge may be applied to cover the additional handling effort. This business process covers the configuration and processing of VAS types and subservice types in the order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, and stock transfer processes. VAS-related costs can be managed using charge codes, which are maintained independently of material pricing and applied as pricing conditions in sales or purchase orders. These codes specify surcharges based on the service’s complexity or resource requirements.

Before starting the repacking process, you can create ad hoc warehouse tasks to move the products / handling units to be repacked to the clarification zone. At the end of the process, you move the repacked products / handling units to the final bin. There are different use cases for repacking: • Pack stock into a handling unit • Repack stock from one handling unit into another handling unit • Unpack stock from one handling unit onto the bin

processes.name: Warehouse Kanban Supply into Production
processes.overview: This scope item allows you to replenish material from your warehouse to production. The process starts with a notification of the empty container status in the system. By setting the Kanban status to EMPTY, the system triggers the creation of a warehouse task. A warehouse operative picks the material from the replenishment storage type, moves it to the production supply area storage bin, and confirms the task in the system. The Kanban container status is automatically set to FULL. If the production supply area is not WM-managed, the stock transfer to the production storage location is executed immediately with the confirmation. This helps to keep the manual posting effort to a minimum. Second option: On receipt of the material, the demand source can set the Kanban container status to FULL. The warehouse task is immediately confirmed and the stock transfer to the production storage location is triggered accordingly, if required.

processes.name: Warehouse Outbound Processing
processes.overview: With this process, products are picked, packed, and sent from your warehouse. This scope item supports different outbound process scenarios. For example, you can send ordered products to external customers, return products to suppliers, and supply products to internal customers. The process starts with an outbound delivery that is relevant for processing in the warehouse. Warehouse tasks are created based on the outbound delivery. The physical process for picking is executed and then confirmed. If packing is required, a warehouse worker packs the products into shipping handling units. Serial numbers are captured in different steps depending on whether the product is managed on documentation level (documentation serialization) or stock level (serialization in stock). Finally, the goods issue is posted.

processes.name: Warehouse Physical Inventory
processes.overview: In this scope item, you can plan, conduct, and confirm regular counts of actual product quantities in the warehouse and compare the physical stock to the data in the system. You first create physical inventory documents for a chosen number of storage bins or products or based on cycle counting indicators. The cycle counting method is used to count products at regular intervals during a year. You can set up counting intervals based on cycle count indicators. After the documents are created and printed, you count the stock in the warehouse. You enter the count result in the system and review discrepancies in the system quantities. By posting the PI documents, you adjust the book inventory in the storage bins to align it with the physical inventory counts. The inventory may be recounted until final counts are accepted. Finally, inventory differences are posted to reconcile stocks in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system.

processes.name: Warehouse Production Integration
processes.overview: With this business process, you can integrate the supply of products to production and the receipt of finished products from production into your warehouse. You first trigger the staging of material that is requested by production. This activity results in an outbound delivery that is distributed to the warehouse as an outbound delivery order (non-WM-managed production supply area). Further process steps such as the creation of warehouse tasks are initiated based on these documents. A warehouse operative moves the material to the production supply area and confirms the warehouse tasks accordingly. If the production storage location is not WM-managed, the goods issue must be posted for the outbound delivery to make the material available for consumption at the production storage location. Finally, the finished goods from production – to be stored in the warehouse – are received and moved to the final bin.

processes.name: Warehouse Production Integration with Synchronous Goods Receipt
processes.overview: This scope item describes the integration of warehouse production with synchronous goods receipt, where the produced products can post goods receipts directly into the warehouse without involving delivery documents. With this business process, you can integrate the supply of products to production and the receipt of finished products from production into your warehouse. You first trigger the staging of material that is requested by production. This activity results in a posting change delivery (warehouse-managed production supply area). Further process steps (such as the creation of warehouse tasks) are initiated based on this document. A warehouse operative moves the material to the production supply area and confirms the warehouse tasks accordingly. The produced products can post goods receipts directly into the warehouse without involving delivery documents. Finally, the finished goods from production – to be stored in the warehouse – are moved to the final bin.

processes.name: Warranty Claim Management – Customer Claim Processing
processes.overview: This scenario enables you to create a warranty claim for a reimbursement request of a supplier (based on a performed repair). In this scenario, you create a claim, validate it for completeness and eligibility for reimbursement, and determine the correct prices for material, labor activities, and so on. Based on the validation support of the system, the claim analyst can make a transparent decision on the claim and perform the financial reimbursement to the customer.

processes.name: Warranty Claim Management – Supplier Recovery Processing
processes.overview: This scenario enables you to create a warranty claim that can then be forwarded to the respective supplier for a reimbursement. The scenario covers the relevant steps starting with the creation of a claim (based on a performed repair), continuing with the validation for completeness, eligibility for reimbursement, and the finding of the correct prices for material, labor activities, and so on. Once the information is sent to the supplier and their response is received, the scenario supports the transparent maintenance of values and the posting of the negotiated amount.

processes.name: Wave Management in Warehousing
processes.overview: This scope item allows you to run and optimize the process of creating picking warehouse tasks by using wave management to extend the warehouse outbound process. The process starts with the creation of waves via the schedule background job report, which combines items from the outbound deliveries based on certain criteria. The Warehouse Clerk (EWM) releases the picking waves by using the warehouse monitor. The system determines the location for picking the stock and allocates the stock to the warehouse task. You can also check the log history of wave and warehouse tasks using the warehouse monitor.
